reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more targeted speed work (intervals and tempo runs) alongside longer, aerobic-focused runs, directly addressing the goal of increasing speed and power. Plan B, while including hill work, relies heavily on longer, easier runs, which, while beneficial for endurance, won't provide the same stimulus for improving running economy and speed. Plan A’s structured approach to building speed and lactate threshold is more appropriate for a runner seeking to improve their overall performance.
